system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: A network logon for sam.okafor on WS-ICHEN-01 came from WS-SOKAFOR-01 shortly before the PowerShell activity, consistent with the inventory's stated remote-administration practice.

At 13:42 UTC, PowerShell ran under sam.okafor and invoked the organization's documented Apply-Updates.ps1 path. The command line includes ExecutionPolicy Bypass, but that alone does not establish malicious execution.
The PowerShell process connected through the explicit proxy to download.windowsupdate.com; the proxy records a Windows Update Agent user agent and about 38.8 MB of server-to-client bytes.

PowerShell launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update MSU quietly; wusa.exe and then PowerShell exited shortly afterward. This sequence is consistent with the scheduled workstation patching and documented IT workflow.

The supplied records also show connection attempts from DC-NWD-01 to WS-ICHEN-01 around 13:51 UTC; the recorded attempts to ports 8080, 443, and 445 were rejected, and another attempt to port 135 did not show a completed connection. The records do not link these attempts to the PowerShell execution.

known_telemetry_limitations: The evidence includes the PowerShell command line but not the contents or integrity verification of Apply-Updates.ps1.
The Windows Update proxy record is a CONNECT tunnel with byte counts; the supplied record does not show the downloaded file's hash or contents.
Process-creation records do not establish whether a PowerShell window was visible to ivy.chen.
